story.headline: Why are ultra-processed foods linked to heart disease? New clues found in the bloodstream

carousel.cover_headline:
Ultra-processed food and heart disease:
New clues found
in the bloodstream

slides.label: THE STUDY
slides.headline: **6,010** British civil servants were followed over many years
slides.insight: None had heart disease or diabetes when they gave blood samples.

slides.label: WHAT THEY FOUND
slides.headline: A blood pattern was linked to ultra-processed food consumption
slides.insight: It accounted for about half the link to cardiovascular disease.

slides.label: BEYOND INGREDIENTS
slides.headline: Sugar, salt and fat may not be the whole story
slides.insight: Researchers suggest how food is made may also matter.

slides.label: THE SPLIT
slides.headline: Only **18%** of daily intake was ultra-processed, by weight
slides.insight: Minimally processed food — fruit, vegetables, grains — made up about 62%.

slides.label: TRY THIS WEEK
slides.headline: Swap a packaged snack for a minimally processed option
slides.insight: Fruit, plain water, unsweetened tea or nuts all count.

sources: Whitehall II study / University College London and Imperial College London, 2026 (reported by Earth.com)
carousel.caption:
Ultra-processed food and heart disease: new clues found in the bloodstream

A study of 6,010 British civil servants found a blood pattern linked to ultra-processed food diets — accounting for about half the association with cardiovascular disease. Researchers say processing itself may play a role, beyond just sugar, salt and saturated fat. More research is needed before any firm conclusions can be drawn. Does this change how you think about packaged foods at home?

Not medical advice.

Sources: Whitehall II study / University College London and Imperial College London, 2026 (reported by Earth.com)
